summary: GRAVEYARD expectations/execution pass covered all 12 active-batch companies and kept Earth quality separate from opportunity/timing. Reliable current market-price/consensus data was not established uniformly for the batch in this cycle, so no price target, Opportunity Score or Action State was fabricated. Instead the lane identified the operating expectations each security appears most exposed to: sustained hyperscaler AI capex, product-ramp execution, export-policy stability, backlog conversion, customer concentration and memory-cycle durability. No company is ready_for_chief for T0 from this lane because the queue still carries unresolved company-evidence blockers and comparable valuation inputs are incomplete.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: A favorable investment outcome now requires not only launch/space-systems growth but credible Neutron schedule/economics and disciplined acquisition funding. Narrative upside can outrun execution if both capital demands peak together.
contradictions: Large backlog and strategic expansion support long-run optionality, while cash burn and schedule risk make timing sensitive.
unknowns: Reliable current valuation bridge, post-acquisition diluted shares, normalized FCF and market-implied Neutron success probability.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Execution milestones improve without incremental financing stress while revenue/backlog conversion supports positive operating leverage.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: The market case is likely highly sensitive to sustained triple-digit-like AI connectivity growth and continued hyperscaler wins. Concentration makes even modest customer normalization capable of producing a large expectations reset.
contradictions: Current profitability and growth are exceptional, but customer concentration makes extrapolation fragile.
unknowns: Reliable current valuation multiple, consensus growth path and customer-specific program duration.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Growth remains broad and durable after top-customer concentration falls, reducing the expectations cliff.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Performance warrants tied to up to $6.5B of Amazon purchases create a visible growth bridge but also imply the market can price in customer milestones before diversified revenue is proven.
contradictions: Customer-linked purchasing milestones improve visibility while increasing dependence and dilution/contra-revenue complexity.
unknowns: Current valuation, vesting schedule actually expected by the market and non-Amazon growth contribution.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Non-Amazon growth accelerates enough that customer-linked warrant milestones become secondary to broader adoption.

expectationTest: Execution must clear an unusually high bar: sustained platform leadership, rapid product cadence, cloud-capex durability and manageable China exclusion/custom-silicon substitution. Excellent operations can still disappoint if expectations assume near-frictionless AI infrastructure growth.
contradictions: Business quality is extraordinary, but export restrictions and buyer concentration make the path less linear than headline growth suggests.
unknowns: Uniform current consensus/valuation set, custom-accelerator share expectations and duration of restricted-market exclusion.
falsifier: Growth/margins remain resilient through capex normalization while software ecosystem and system share stay dominant.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: The investment case requires MI-series repeat deployments and software maturity to convert strong Data Center demand into durable accelerator economics; CPU strength alone may not satisfy an AI-rerating thesis.
contradictions: Data Center growth validates demand while accelerator share durability remains less established.
unknowns: Current market-implied MI revenue/share, normalized accelerator margin and customer concentration.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Multiple customers expand MI deployments with sustained margins and improving software stickiness.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: AI custom-silicon growth and VMware cash generation support the narrative, but concentration means a small number of program decisions can change incremental growth rapidly. Deleveraging helps execution credibility but cannot eliminate customer-program risk.
contradictions: Strong FCF improves downside resilience while concentrated AI/custom programs raise earnings sensitivity.
unknowns: Current valuation/consensus AI revenue, customer-level program duration and normalized post-VMware tax/refinancing burden.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: AI program breadth increases and leverage falls while no large customer meaningfully reduces custom-silicon demand.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: A high-quality foundry thesis can still face execution drag if overseas-fab costs widen faster than pricing and resilience premiums. The market must balance advanced-node scarcity against geopolitical and structural-cost discounts.
contradictions: Resilience capex lowers tail risk but raises near/mid-term margin dilution.
unknowns: Current geopolitical discount embedded in valuation, customer willingness to pay resilience premiums and overseas yield convergence.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Overseas dilution stays within or below guide while advanced-node pricing/volume offsets cost and geopolitical risk does not impair utilization.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: The market can rationally pay for monopoly-like EUV scarcity, but execution still depends on customer capex timing, High-NA ROI and export-policy stability. China mix gives policy shocks a direct revenue channel.
contradictions: Scarcity and technology leadership support premium expectations while policy and cyclicality can create order volatility.
unknowns: Current valuation/consensus order path, 2026 China mix and High-NA utilization economics at customer scale.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Order growth stays strong despite lower China mix and High-NA adoption proves economically compelling across multiple customers.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: The investment thesis needs royalty growth and new compute-platform monetization to outrun concentration/related-party discounts. Asset-light economics can support high expectations, but governance/customer mix may cap how much premium is justified.
contradictions: Royalty growth is strong while 57% top-five concentration and rising related-party revenue reduce independence.
unknowns: Current valuation, AGI CPU contribution expectations, SoftBank-related commercial assumptions and RISC-V substitution path.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: External royalty growth broadens, related-party mix normalizes and new compute products scale without margin or governance compromise.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: Execution risk is classic memory-cycle asymmetry: investors can mistake peak HBM scarcity earnings for normalized economics while a very large capex program expands fixed-cost exposure. Durable long-term contracts and technology lead would justify a higher trough multiple only if supply discipline persists.
contradictions: AI memory demand is structurally strong, but memory remains capital intensive and supply responsive.
unknowns: Current through-cycle valuation, HBM4 market-share assumptions, contract floors and normalized FCF after expansion.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: HBM pricing, share and margins remain resilient through capacity additions with healthy FCF and balance sheet.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: Strong margins, cash flow and AI networking exposure support quality, but cloud-titan concentration means expectations can reset quickly on architecture changes or slower capex. XPO/1.6T success must broaden across buyers to reduce this execution risk.
contradictions: Excellent customer satisfaction and innovation coexist with concentration and proprietary-fabric substitution risk.
unknowns: Current top-customer share, market-implied AI networking growth and buyer breadth for new platforms.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Customer mix broadens while new networking platforms scale across multiple cloud/enterprise buyers with stable margins.

ready_for_chief.expectationTest: A very large backlog supports strong forward demand expectations, but investment timing depends on conversion quality, customer project timing and power/interconnection availability. Raw book-to-bill can overstate near-term realizable earnings if cancellations/reschedules rise.
contradictions: Demand is real while backlog timing/terms create execution uncertainty.
unknowns: Current valuation/consensus backlog conversion, cancellation rates, customer concentration and margin by backlog vintage.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule at stable/improving margins with low cancellations and broad customer participation.

materialFindings.finding: The dominant expectations risk across the batch is common: sustained hyperscaler AI capex is implicitly required by NVDA, AMD, AVGO, CRDO, ALAB, ANET, TSM, ASML, MU and VRT in different parts of the stack.

Business quality and opportunity must remain separate: several names can be excellent companies yet poor entries if current prices already capitalize perfect execution. Reliable batch-wide current price/consensus data was not established here, so no fabricated Opportunity/Execution scores were produced.

Execution variables that deserve explicit future calibration include ALAB customer-warrant vesting, TSM overseas-fab dilution, MU HBM/capex normalization, RKLB Neutron/acquisition funding and VRT backlog conversion.

contradictions: High Earth-quality businesses can still have poor execution asymmetry when expectations are already extreme.
Geographic resilience can lower tail risk while worsening near-term margins/capital intensity.
Customer-linked purchase commitments can improve visibility while increasing buyer power and dilution complexity.
unknowns: No uniform timestamped current-price/market-cap/consensus dataset was established for all 12 names in this cycle.
Opportunity Score, Execution Score and Action State therefore remain unknown rather than inferred.
Comparable market-implied growth assumptions are not normalized across the batch.

peerRequests.request: Close operational blockers first; expectations should not substitute for missing concentration, diluted-share, backlog-quality or cash-runway evidence.
When reliable timestamped market/consensus sources are available, preserve provenance so valuation/execution can be reproduced without contaminating Earth Score.

accuracyDebates.reason: The batch contains multiple layers of one spending chain; correlated expectations should be calibrated as a portfolio/common-shock risk.
Uniform current market/consensus inputs were not established, so leaving opportunity/action state unknown is more accurate than proxying from stale prices.
